explanation.headline: You ate 6.85 mg of iron but absorbed about 0.016 mg, mainly because of the black tea.

points.text: Black tea polyphenols cut non-haem iron absorption by about 87%.
Phytate in the lentils and rice also lowers absorption.

explanation.tip: Have your tea at least an hour after eating.

conflicts.message: Black tea with this meal can cut the non-haem iron you absorb by about 86%. Having it at least an hour after eating reduces this effect.

ABS_BASE_IRON_006.summary: Monsen and Balintfy (1982): available non-haem iron % = 3 + 8.93 x ln((EF + 100) / 100) for EF < 75, and 8% for EF >= 75, where EF = g meat/fish/poultry + mg ascorbic acid in the meal. Continuous refinement of the 3/5/8% categories of Monsen et al. (1978).

evidence.notes: Used as the per-meal non-haem base before inhibitor modifiers.

paper.title: Calculating dietary iron bioavailability: refinement and computerization
paper.journal: Journal of the American Dietetic Association

evidence.notes: Unit tests check the continuous form matches 3% at 0 and 8% at 75 enhancer units.

paper.authors: Monsen ER, Hallberg L, Layrisse M, et al.
paper.title: Estimation of available dietary iron

evidence.notes: Black tea 79-94% reduction (abstract). Per-serving polyphenol values to extract from Table 1.

ASSUME_002.description: Phytate phosphorus = 28.2% of phytic acid mass.
ASSUME_002.rationale: Stoichiometry: 6 P atoms (6 x 30.97) in phytic acid (660.04 g/mol). Converts PhyFoodComp phytate mg to the phytate P doses used by Hallberg 1989.

papers.authors: Hallberg L, Brune M, Rossander L
papers.title: Iron absorption in man: ascorbic acid and dose-dependent inhibition by phytate

ASSUME_005.description: Proportion of phytate inhibition removed = min(1, vitamin C mg / (30 x max(1, phytate P mg / 58))).
ASSUME_005.rationale: Siegenberg 1991: 30 mg ascorbic acid overcame inhibition from up to 58 mg phytate P. Linear scaling outside that is an assumption.

papers.authors: Siegenberg D, Baynes RD, Bothwell TH, et al.
papers.title: Ascorbic acid prevents the dose-dependent inhibitory effects of polyphenols and phytates on nonheme-iron absorption

ASSUME_006.description: Calcium effect rises linearly from 0% at 0 mg to the 165 mg range; 165-600 mg uses the 50-60% range; held above 600 mg.
ASSUME_006.rationale: Hallberg 1991 reports dose-related inhibition from 40 mg; the abstract gives figures only at 165 mg and 300-600 mg.

papers.authors: Hallberg L, Brune M, Erlandsson M, Sandberg AS, Rossander-Hultén L
papers.title: Calcium: effect of different amounts on nonheme- and heme-iron absorption in humans

ASSUME_013.description: Vitamin C used to counteract phytate (up to 30 mg per 58 mg phytate P) does not also count as a Monsen enhancer.
ASSUME_013.rationale: Siegenberg 1991: 30 mg ascorbic acid with phytate gave the same absorption as the plain meal, not more. Avoids counting vitamin C twice.
